hero.image_alt: Two porcelain robots play chess at a walnut table in a sunlit marble hall.
hero.lead: Take your seat at a waxed walnut table in a sunlit royal hall. Across the board, a porcelain robot driven by Stockfish waits for your first move.
hero.meta: Free software · Windows, Linux, macOS (experimental) · Graphics card with OpenGL 4.6
hero.caption: Captured in the game: the title screen

experience.title:
Not a board on a screen.
A seat at the table.
experience.lead: Scacelith brings back what makes a real game: the hall, the silence, the clock, an opponent who looks at you, and the rituals of the tournament.

presence.title: In the first person
presence.text: You see through your robot's eyes: look around the hall, lean over the board, look up at your opponent, glance at your scoresheet, or stand and walk to an end of the table.

ritual.title: Tournament rules
ritual.text: A piece you touch must be moved, and your hand presses the clock to complete the move. With the move hints off, the arbiter penalises an illegal move, and a second one loses the game.

scoresheet.title: Written by hand
scoresheet.text: Both players record every move on their own scoresheet, each in a handwriting of their own, and turn the page every forty moves. You hear the pen on the paper.

opponent.title: A worthy opponent
opponent.text: Stockfish 19 at your level, from Novice (800) to Stockfish Max (3500), with a rating computed by the FIDE rules after every game.

engine.title: Built for this game
engine.text: An engine written from scratch: physically based light, marble, waxed wood, porcelain and brass, the sun through the windows, soft shadows and reflections. Quality presets, from Very low to Ultra, fit it to your graphics card.

languages.title: Ten languages
languages.text: English, French, German, Spanish, Ukrainian, Russian, Arabic, Japanese and Chinese, simplified and traditional. Arabic is laid out right to left.

modes.title:
Every game
has its table.
modes.lead: Everything is played in the same hall, from the title screen. Offline, Stockfish is always ready for a game.

new_game.name: New Game
new_game.text: Face Stockfish at the strength of your choice, with a time control from bullet to classical, or play a friend on the same computer, each from their own robot's eyes.

coach.name: Coach
coach.text: A teacher sits across from you, plays at your level and talks you through the game: threats, good moves, mistakes, playing out with its own hand what a mistake costs. From the rules of chess to expert level, with a voice synthesised on your computer.

challenges.name: Coach Challenges
challenges.text: Short sets of positions, each training one skill: mates in one to three, forks, pins and other tactics, defence, and the basic endgames against the coach. Hints only when you ask, and a green check for every set you complete.

analysis.name: Analysis
analysis.text: Stockfish reviews your saved games, your online games or any PGN: an evaluation bar, the key moves marked from brilliant to blunder, the better move drawn as an arrow, and comments aloud and in subtitles. The robots' hands play the moves as you step through.

online.name: Play Online
online.text: Real opponents through a Scacelith server: rated games, matchmaking, challenges and private games, or a direct match between two computers. Your opponent's robot moves with them, live.

watch.name: Watch a Game
watch.text: Two Stockfish players face each other while you move freely around the hall, invisible, from one viewpoint to another.

saved.name: Saved Games
saved.text: Your games are kept as PGN files. Replay them in the hall, with the real thinking times and clocks, or bring in games from other programs.

gallery.title: Seen from inside the hall
gallery.lead: Every picture is captured in the game, in real time, by its own engine.

online.title:
Real opponents,
the same hall.
online.lead: Sign in to the official server from the game and play people from everywhere, still in the first person.
online.point_rated: Rated games in every official time control, each with its own rating, computed by FIDE's rules.
online.point_match: Matchmaking, challenges by name and private games with a code; or a direct match between two computers, with no server or account.
online.point_fair: Fair play: automatic checks, engine analysis of finished games and player reports.
online.point_history: Your game history on this site: download each game as PGN or as an animated GIF.
online.point_open: Anyone can run a community server: the server is free software, and its API is documented.

download.title:
Take your seat.
Free, and open source.
download.lead: Unpack and play: no installer on Windows or Linux, and a drag to Applications on a Mac. Every file is built from its tagged source by GitHub Actions, with an attested build provenance.
download.macos_note: For Apple Silicon Macs (M1 or later) with macOS 26 or later, not in a virtual machine; newer and less tested than the other builds. The app is not signed by a registered Apple developer: the first time, open it from System Settings › Privacy & Security › Open Anyway.
download.req_system_value: Windows 64-bit (x64); Linux 64-bit (x86-64 or aarch64) with glibc 2.34, OpenSSL 3 and X11 or XWayland, such as Ubuntu 22.04 or Debian 12; macOS 26 or later on Apple Silicon (experimental)
download.req_gpu_value: A graphics card with OpenGL 4.6 and an up-to-date driver (on a Mac, the game brings its own OpenGL)
download.req_included_value: Stockfish 19 and its neural network: play offline right away
download.req_network_value: For online play, GIFs, and the voice of the coach and of the analysis (an optional download of about 399 MB)
download.verify_text: Each file's build provenance is attested by GitHub. With the GitHub CLI:

credits.title: Credits and thanks
credits.engine: Stockfish 19, by the Stockfish developers (GNU GPL v3). Its neural network was trained on data provided by the Leela Chess Zero project (Open Database License).
credits.voice: Supertonic 3 by Supertone, under the BigScience Open RAIL-M licence: downloaded at your request, it speaks for the coach and the analysis, on your computer.
credits.fonts: EB Garamond by Georg Duffner, Cinzel by Natanael Gama and Amiri by Khaled Hosny; handwriting in Caveat, Marck Script, Bad Script, Aref Ruqaa, Klee One and LXGW WenKai (all SIL Open Font License); chess figures from GNU FreeFont.
credits.openings: Opening names from the chess-openings database of lichess.org, and the puzzles of the coach's challenges from the Lichess puzzle database, both dedicated to the public domain (CC0).

legal.lead: Who publishes and hosts Scacelith, what happens to your data on this website, in the game and on the official server, and the rules for playing there.

notice.title: Legal notice
notice.publisher: Scacelith is published by a private individual, on a non-professional basis. As French law allows (article 1-1 II of law no. 2004-575 of 21 June 2004), the publisher's identity is not shown here; it is known to the hosting provider.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.intro: Scacelith shows no advertising, sells no data and measures no audience. Personal data is used only to run this website and the official server, as described below. The controller is the publisher, reachable at the contact address above.
privacy.site_hosting: GitHub hosts the site and, like any web host, records visitors' IP addresses for security purposes.
privacy.site_requests: To show the newest release, your browser asks GitHub's API (api.github.com); to show the server's status, the leaderboard, players and your account, it asks the official server (caissa.scacelith.com). Both receive your IP address, as with any request.
privacy.site_storage: The site sets no cookies and has no analytics. It keeps in your browser only your choice of language and, once you sign in, your session: for the current tab only, or on this device if you tick “Keep me signed in”. Both are needed for the site to work, and the session is sent only to the official server.
privacy.site_trailer: The trailer is a YouTube video. Nothing is loaded from YouTube until you press “Accept and play”; YouTube (Google) then receives your IP address and may store cookies or other trackers on your device. Your answer is not remembered: the question comes back at your next visit.
privacy.game_local: The game keeps its settings, your local results and your sign-in on your computer. The sign-in is kept in the system's secure store: DPAPI on Windows, the Keychain on macOS, the Secret Service keyring on Linux, or else a file that only your user account can read.
privacy.game_network: It sends nothing on its own: no telemetry, no update check. It connects to the official server only when you open the online page, to Hugging Face only when you download the coach's voice, and, for a direct match, to your opponent's computer, which then knows your IP address (the game may also open a port on your router with UPnP).
privacy.account_title: Your account on the official server
privacy.account_intro: Creating an account, in the game or on this website, and playing online send the following data to the official server, hosted by OVH in France:
privacy.data_account: Account: user name, e-mail address, password (stored only as an Argon2id hash), two-step verification secret (encrypted) and recovery codes (hashed), sign-up date and date of last sign-in.
privacy.data_google: Sign in with Google: Google sends your Google account identifier, your e-mail address and your name. The server keeps the identifier and the address, and uses the name only to suggest a user name.
privacy.data_sessions: Signed-in devices: for each sign-in, the name of the device (the game's version and system, such as “Scacelith/1.0.0 win64”, or the browser and system for this website), the IP address and the dates of use.
privacy.data_games: Games and ratings: every online game (players, moves, time spent on each move, result, dates) and your ratings. During a game, the movements of your head and hand are relayed live to your opponent and never stored.
privacy.data_security: Security log: sign-ins, failed attempts and changes to the account, with the IP address.
privacy.data_fairplay: Fair play: reports filed by you or about you, with their comment; abandoned and missed games; sanctions; and the checks run on games, from forged or impossible moves to statistics from the Stockfish engine.
privacy.basis_title: Why, and on what legal basis
privacy.basis_contract: Running your account and online play (sign-in, matches, ratings, game records, the e-mails the service sends): the service you sign up for (article 6(1)(b) GDPR).
privacy.basis_security: Protecting accounts and the server, and keeping games fair (security log, IP addresses, fair-play checks, sanctions): the legitimate interest of the publisher and of the players (article 6(1)(f) GDPR).
privacy.basis_trailer: Playing the trailer from YouTube: your consent, given with the button (article 6(1)(a) GDPR).
privacy.public: Your user name, sign-up date, ratings and full list of games, with every move, are public: on this website, through the server's API and in each game's PGN. Your e-mail address, devices, sign-ins, sanctions and fair-play records are never shown. You can refuse direct challenges, but games cannot be hidden.
privacy.auto: Some breaches of the game's protocol, such as a forged message or a move that is impossible in the position, are certain proof of cheating: the server then forfeits the game, bans the account for 24 hours, removes it from the leaderboard and gives back the points its opponents lost to it in the last 60 days. Three games abandoned, aborted or missed in 24 hours pause rated matchmaking for 15 minutes, then longer. Engine statistics never lead to a sanction on their own: a person decides. You can ask for any decision to be reviewed at the contact address.
privacy.recipient_ovh: OVH SAS hosts the server and its data, in France.
privacy.recipient_scaleway: Scaleway SAS (8 rue de la Ville-l'Évêque, 75008 Paris, France) sends the server's e-mails: it receives your address, your user name and the message.
privacy.recipient_google: Google receives what your browser sends it when you choose to sign in with Google, under its own privacy policy.
privacy.recipient_staff: The server's administrator and moderators see account and fair-play data to run the service.
privacy.recipient_players: Other players see what is public, and your opponent sees your moves and movements during a game.
privacy.recipient_none: No one else: no data is sold, rented or used for advertising.
privacy.transfers: Account data stays in France. GitHub, Google and Porkbun (which forwards messages sent to the contact address) are based in the United States: what they receive falls under their own policies and their safeguards for transfers out of the European Union.
privacy.ret_account: Account: until you delete it. A sign-up whose address is never confirmed is deleted after 24 hours.
privacy.ret_sessions: Signed-in devices: until you sign out, after 30 days without use, and after 90 days at most.
privacy.ret_ip: IP addresses: erased after 30 days. The server's logs keep only shortened addresses.
privacy.ret_games: Games and ratings: as long as the server keeps its game records, which are also your opponents' records. Once your account is deleted, your name in them is replaced by “deleted#” and a number.
privacy.ret_fairplay: Sanctions, reports and fair-play results: kept, so that banned players cannot simply come back and other players stay protected. Once your account is deleted, they remain linked only to its number.
privacy.ret_backups: Backups: deleted data can remain for a short time in the server's backup copy, until it is replaced.
privacy.ret_contact: Messages to the contact address: as long as needed to answer them.
privacy.rights: You can access, correct, erase and export your data, restrict its use and object to it (articles 15 to 21 GDPR).
privacy.rights_self: Most of this is in your account, in the game or on this website's Account page: download your account data as a JSON file, change your e-mail address or password, sign out other devices, or delete the account at once.
privacy.rights_google: An account created with Google has no password: to export or delete it, first give it one with “Forgot password?”.
privacy.rights_mail: For anything else, including data the export does not contain (fair-play checks, reports about you), write to the contact address. You will get an answer within one month.
privacy.rights_cnil: If you think your rights are not respected, you can lodge a complaint with the CNIL (3 place de Fontenoy, TSA 80715, 75334 Paris Cedex 07, France) or with the data protection authority of your country.

terms.title: Terms of use
terms.intro: These terms apply to the official server (caissa.scacelith.com) and to the account pages of this website. Creating an account or playing on the official server means accepting them.
terms.service: A free service. The game is free software, free of charge. The official server is offered free of charge and as is, with no guarantee of availability: it can change, stop for a while or close.
terms.account: Your account. You are responsible for what is done with it and for keeping its password secret. Write to the contact address at once if you think someone else uses it.
terms.username: Your user name is public: it must not be offensive or hateful, impersonate someone or reveal anyone's personal data.
terms.fair: Fair play. During a rated game, no help from a chess engine, another person or any other tool. No modified game client, forged messages or deliberate overloading of the server.
terms.conduct: Finish your games. Abandoning or aborting games, or missing games you were matched for, three times in 24 hours pauses rated matchmaking for a while.
terms.reports: Reports must be made in good faith. To report a player or illegal content, such as an offensive user name, use the report button of a game or write to the contact address.
terms.sanctions: Sanctions. Breaking these rules can lead to a forfeit, a warning, a ban and removal from the leaderboard; points lost to a cheater are given back to their opponents. Only certain proof of cheating is sanctioned automatically; anything else is decided by a person. You can contest a sanction at the contact address.
terms.liability: Liability. Within the limits allowed by law, the publisher is not liable for interruptions of the service or for the loss of games, ratings or data.
terms.end: Ending. You can delete your account at any time. An account that breaks these terms can be banned.
terms.changes: Changes. These terms can change; the date at the top of this page shows the current version, and playing on after a change means accepting it.
terms.law: Law. These terms are governed by French law. In case of a dispute, write first to the contact address to find a solution together.
